Step 1 · Predict: when does it run?

The component has already mounted. You click +1. Which effects run?

src/ThreeEffects.jsx
  1. import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
  3. export default function ThreeEffects() {
  4. const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  5. const [name, setName] = useState('');
  7. useEffect(() => { console.log('A: no array'); });
  8. useEffect(() => { console.log('B: empty array'); }, []);
  9. useEffect(() => { console.log('C: depends on count'); }, [count]);
  11. return (
  12. <div>
  13. <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>+1</button>
  14. <input value={name} onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)} />
  15. <p>{count}</p>
  16. </div>
  17. );
  18. }
Correct. A runs after every render. C runs because count changed. B runs only on mount.
Incorrect. Look at each option and try again.

Step 2 · Run in Cursor

Your task

Fetch the data from the API https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users and show the first user's name.

  1. Create src/FirstUser.jsx with a state that starts as null.
  2. Do the fetch inside a useEffect with an empty array.
  3. While there is no data, show "Loading...".
  4. Add it to App.jsx.

Step 3 · Compare

Which name does your screen show?

Correct.
Not a match. That is user 2. /users returns a list: the first one is [0].
Not a match. Check that you show .name of element [0] of the list.

Step 3 · Compare

One possible solution

src/FirstUser.jsx
  1. import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
  3. export default function FirstUser() {
  4. const [users, setUsers] = useState(null);
  6. useEffect(() => {
  7. fetch('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users')
  8. .then((res) => res.json())
  9. .then((data) => setUsers(data));
  10. }, []);
  12. return <p>{users ? users[0].name : 'Loading...'}</p>;
  13. }
In the Network tab you will see 2 requests in development: that is StrictMode.

Step 3 · Compare

In short

  • The array decides when. No array: every render. []: on mount. [x]: when x changes.
  • A fetch with no array never stops.
  • In development, every mount effect runs twice.
